headline: US hitting Iran 'economically and militarily'
dek: Trump: US continues hitting Iran hard 'economically and militarily'; praised Putin for 'laying off of Iran' and China for doing little; hinted at hostage-release breakthrough ('you'll see soon enough'); defended continued Putin negotiations; criticized NATO (US 'asked for help in Iran, help which…
sources: Trump remarks (Times of India/ET Now carry); Axios (2 sources) on Hegseth-Netanyahu meeting
fault_line: Trump and Netanyahu: united front against Iran — or a wartime alliance running on borrowed time before the midterms?

sections.what_happened: Trump: US continues hitting Iran hard 'economically and militarily'; praised Putin for 'laying off of Iran' and China for doing little; hinted at hostage-release breakthrough ('you'll see soon enough'); defended continued Putin negotiations; criticized NATO (US 'asked for help in Iran, help which we didn't need, but I was testing Nato'). Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth met Netanyahu in unannounced Monday Israel visit (Axios, 2 sources). Monday Trump-Netanyahu phone call (released by Netanyahu): Trump predicted 'tremendous' election victory for Netanyahu next week (Oct 27 vote); Netanyahu called Trump 'by far, the greatest friend Israel has ever had'.
sections.what_verified: Times of India, ET Now, TimesNow liveblog, Axios (Hegseth), Gulf News (call). Trump-NATO line via Times of India carry.
sections.what_disputed: Trump's 'Russia doing nothing for Iran' contradicts Lavrov's Tehran pledges and the trade data (see 0700-03) — flag the contradiction on screen. Hegseth visit agenda unconfirmed. 'Hostage soon' = Trump's claim only (Stephen Hubbard context from prior scans).
sections.why_matters: Washington says it's hitting Iran hard — while Beijing and Moscow are 'doing nothing'. The receipts from Tehran and Dushanbe say otherwise.
sections.context: Background: Trump: US hitting Iran 'economically and militarily'; Hegseth makes unannounced Israel visit; Trump-Netanyahu call

totw_analysis: Our read: Washington says it's hitting Iran hard — while Beijing and Moscow are 'doing nothing'. The receipts from Tehran and Dushanbe say otherwise. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Trump and Netanyahu: united front against Iran — or a wartime alliance running on borrowed time before the midterms?
